correctness.rationale: For every finite k,l>=2 and m,n>=1, coordinate central elements force each bounded Heyting map into a chain to factor through one source coordinate. Constancy under either global quantifier forces a shared chain homomorphism; one-hot existential or one-zero universal tests force surjectivity of the coordinate map. Conversely a common chain map and a surjection preserve both extrema. Implication preservation forces strict chain growth below top and classifies all chain maps by subsets of interior target levels. Surjection and subset counts yield all enumerations; idempotents require prefix-fixing threshold maps. Edge cases k=2, l=2, m=1, n<m were explicitly checked. A standalone operation-table verifier independently checked small cases and image-rank distributions.

value.rationale: This is the complete finite cross-parameter morphism category for a natural full functional semantics of one-variable Gödel logic, not a selected case or simple term closure. It identifies the sharp no-downward-coordinate morphism obstruction, proves either global quantifier alone imposes both quantifier laws on bounded Heyting homomorphisms, and converts all hom-set, image-rank and idempotent questions into exact Stirling/binomial data. Those structural and census facts motivate the invariant independently of computation. The result has a precise finite scope and is not presented as a general theorem about all monadic Gödel algebras.
